citation_positions.paragraph: Program transformations are commonly justified by relational correctness arguments. Abstract interpretation provides a systematic language for sound approximations and transformations \cite{cousot1977}. Relational program logics can prove that transformations preserve specified observations \cite{benton2004}. Secure-compilation criteria strengthen correctness by requiring target contexts not to introduce source-impossible behaviors; trace-relating formulations make the source-target observation relation explicit \cite{abate2021}. Robustly safe compilation focuses on preserving safety properties against adversarial contexts \cite{patrignani2021}.

Work on fully abstract compilation includes JavaScript \cite{fournet2013}.
Related approaches use universal embedding \cite{new2016}. A separate line
of work develops modular approximate back-translation \cite{devriese2017}. Robust property preservation classifies guarantees surviving
target contexts \cite{abate2019}. Secure-compilation criteria also address
safety hyperproperties \cite{patrignani2017hyper}. Robust safety is another
such criterion \cite{patrignani2021}. Trace-relating correctness permits different source and
target observation alphabets \cite{abate2021}. Constant-resource compilation
preserves a resource-sensitive relation \cite{barthe2021}. Universal
composability has been characterized through robust compilation in a
cryptographic setting \cite{patrignani2024uc}. Lanckriet et al.\ relate robust
properties, abstraction maps and back-translations across these criteria
\cite{lanckriet2026}. Hyperproperties concern guarantees over sets of traces
rather than ordinary trace properties \cite{clarkson2010}.

citation_positions.paragraph:
Contextual equivalence is the kernel of the observations allowed by a language
contract. Operational accounts of functional languages made contextual
behavior a primary semantic object \cite{plotkin1977}. Full abstraction
requires denotational equality to coincide with contextual equality
\cite{milner1977}. For lazy lambda calculus, convergence-based contextual
equivalence makes the allowed program tests explicit \cite{abramsky1990lazy}. Equivalence
for effectful functional languages shows that the chosen effects materially
change it \cite{mason1991}. Testing equivalence exposes the experiment class
directly for processes \cite{denicola1984}. Algebraic laws for nondeterminism
characterize consequences of those observations compositionally
\cite{hennessy1985}.

current_attributed_claims:
For lazy lambda calculus, convergence-based contextual
equivalence makes the allowed program tests explicit \cite{abramsky1990lazy}.

citation_positions.paragraph: Cryptographic watermarking demonstrates why approximate and computational contracts require separate analysis. Cohen et al.\ obtain watermarking for cryptographic capabilities under assumptions and relaxed correctness, while also extending impossibility results \cite{cohen2018}. The virtual-black-box obfuscation impossibility literature likewise distinguishes what is observable from code and from black-box access \cite{barak2012}. Our theorems do not imply those computational results. They locate a simpler exact semantic bottleneck that applies before computational hardness is considered.

Cryptographic watermarking formalizes correctness and unremovability against
computationally bounded keyed adversaries \cite{cohen2018}. General
obfuscation impossibility results use computational definitions and specially
constructed program families \cite{barak2012}. Our classifications are
extensional preconditions: an uncolorable fixed-key quotient or access
hypergraph rules out the exact channel before efficiency or cryptographic
hardness is considered.

The virtual-black-box obfuscation impossibility literature likewise distinguishes what is observable from code and from black-box access \cite{barak2012}. Our theorems do not imply those computational results. They locate a simpler exact semantic bottleneck that applies before computational hardness is considered.

Cryptographic watermarking formalizes correctness and unremovability against
computationally bounded keyed adversaries \cite{cohen2018}. General
obfuscation impossibility results use computational definitions and specially
constructed program families \cite{barak2012}. Our classifications are
extensional preconditions: an uncolorable fixed-key quotient or access
hypergraph rules out the exact channel before efficiency or cryptographic
hardness is considered.

citation_positions.paragraph:
Work on fully abstract compilation includes JavaScript \cite{fournet2013}.
Related approaches use universal embedding \cite{new2016}. A separate line
of work develops modular approximate back-translation \cite{devriese2017}. Robust property preservation classifies guarantees surviving
target contexts \cite{abate2019}. Secure-compilation criteria also address
safety hyperproperties \cite{patrignani2017hyper}. Robust safety is another
such criterion \cite{patrignani2021}. Trace-relating correctness permits different source and
target observation alphabets \cite{abate2021}. Constant-resource compilation
preserves a resource-sensitive relation \cite{barthe2021}. Universal
composability has been characterized through robust compilation in a
cryptographic setting \cite{patrignani2024uc}. Lanckriet et al.\ relate robust
properties, abstraction maps and back-translations across these criteria
\cite{lanckriet2026}. Hyperproperties concern guarantees over sets of traces
rather than ordinary trace properties \cite{clarkson2010}.

citation_positions.paragraph:
Full abstraction has long served as a compiler-security criterion. A compiler
to JavaScript was proved fully abstract by mediating source and target
observations \cite{fournet2013}. Universal embedding gave a reusable
construction principle \cite{new2016}. Approximate back-translation made full
abstraction modular when exact target-to-source simulation was unavailable
\cite{devriese2017}. Robust property preservation broadened the design space by
classifying property classes that survive arbitrary target contexts
\cite{abate2019}. Secure compilation and hyperproperty preservation made the
connection to safety hyperproperties explicit \cite{patrignani2017hyper}.
Robustly safe compilation isolated a criterion focused on robust safety
\cite{patrignani2021}. Trace-relating correctness permits different source and
target observation alphabets \cite{abate2021}. Constant-resource compilation
preserves a resource-sensitive relation rather than only functionality
\cite{barthe2021}. Universal composability has been characterized through
robust compilation in a cryptographic setting \cite{patrignani2024uc}. A
recent synthesis relates robust properties, abstraction maps, and
back-translations across these criteria \cite{lanckriet2026}.

Constant-resource compilation
preserves a resource-sensitive relation rather than only functionality
\cite{barthe2021}.

citation_positions.paragraph: Program transformations are commonly justified by relational correctness arguments. Abstract interpretation provides a systematic language for sound approximations and transformations \cite{cousot1977}. Relational program logics can prove that transformations preserve specified observations \cite{benton2004}. Secure-compilation criteria strengthen correctness by requiring target contexts not to introduce source-impossible behaviors; trace-relating formulations make the source-target observation relation explicit \cite{abate2021}. Robustly safe compilation focuses on preserving safety properties against adversarial contexts \cite{patrignani2021}.

Abstract interpretation gives a lattice-theoretic account of sound
approximation \cite{cousot1977}. Systematic analysis separates a concrete
semantics, an abstraction, and justified transfer functions \cite{cousot1979}.
The same methodology organizes semantics-preserving transformations
\cite{cousot2002}. Relational proofs can establish that a transformation
preserves the client-selected semantics \cite{benton2004}. Such a proof
discharges $B$ or $\Beh$; it does not determine the implementation image $R$.

Relational proofs can establish that a transformation
preserves the client-selected semantics \cite{benton2004}.

citation_positions.paragraph: Program transformations are commonly justified by relational correctness arguments. Abstract interpretation provides a systematic language for sound approximations and transformations \cite{cousot1977}. Relational program logics can prove that transformations preserve specified observations \cite{benton2004}. Secure-compilation criteria strengthen correctness by requiring target contexts not to introduce source-impossible behaviors; trace-relating formulations make the source-target observation relation explicit \cite{abate2021}. Robustly safe compilation focuses on preserving safety properties against adversarial contexts \cite{patrignani2021}.

Abstract interpretation gives a lattice-theoretic account of sound
approximation \cite{cousot1977}. Systematic analysis separates a concrete
semantics, an abstraction, and justified transfer functions \cite{cousot1979}.
The same methodology organizes semantics-preserving transformations
\cite{cousot2002}. Relational proofs can establish that a transformation
preserves the client-selected semantics \cite{benton2004}. Such a proof
discharges $B$ or $\Beh$; it does not determine the implementation image $R$.

citation_positions.paragraph: When $\equiv_J$ refines $\Beh$ and every source can reach its whole behavior class, observational capacity has a local formula: the minimum number of operational classes contained in a behavior class. In the general case, behavior classes or source-reachability sets overlap the operational quotient. Exact feasibility is then one polychromatic coloring shared by all constraints. Polychromatic coloring is a standard combinatorial object \cite{bollobas2013}; the contribution is the semantics-to-incidence correspondence and its converse. A deterministic terminating language with erased static annotations realizes every nonempty-edge hypergraph, so no stronger local test follows from contextual equivalence alone. The same representation exposes a bipartite two-class fragment, NP-completeness at three classes, and the boundary at which finite counterexamples cease to suffice.

The coloring in Equation~\eqref{eq:polychromatic} is a standard
\emph{polychromatic coloring}: every hyperedge must contain every color.  Its
maximum possible number of colors is the \emph{polychromatic number} of the
hypergraph \cite{bollobas2013}.  This established invariant gives the semantic
contribution its target: the exact identification of robust
watermark capacity with that invariant for the incidence structure generated
by behavior preservation, detector resolution, and attack closure.

The transversal-partition formulation is standard: it is precisely dual cover decomposition, with $\pc(H)=\operatorname{cd}(H^*)$ for the incidence dual $H^*$ \cite{bollobas2013}. In the source interpretation, cell $J$ covers the sources whose access edge contains $J$; each message fiber must cover all sources. The proposition records that existing combinatorial statement in decoder notation.

The exponent below also follows from known cover-decomposition bounds. Dualizing Theorem~1 of Bollob\'{a}s et al. gives a lower bound with minimum edge size in the numerator and $\ln\Delta+O(\ln\ln\Delta)$ in the denominator, where $\Delta$ is maximum vertex degree \cite{bollobas2013}. Applied to powers with minimum edge size $w^n$ and maximum degree $\Delta^n$, it gives $w^n/(n\ln\Delta+O(\ln n))$ colors asymptotically when $\Delta\geq2$. If $\Delta=1$, the edges are disjoint and their minimum size is attainable directly. Together with the width upper bound these already give the same exponent. We supply an elementary union-bound proof and state the semantic product premises explicitly.

The crossing and access classifications use polychromatic hypergraph coloring,
which places every color in every edge \cite{bollobas2013}. Positive
not-all-equal satisfiability supplies the standard hardness source
\cite{schaefer1978}. Restricted positive variants retain hardness under simple
clause shapes \cite{darmann2020}. These established results supply the combinatorial tools for the semantic classification.
Decoder fibers as transversal partitions are the dual cover-decomposition formulation, not a separate invariant. The product exponent follows already from the general minimum-degree/maximum-edge-size cover bound and duality \cite{bollobas2013}. Li and Zhang formulate polychromatic coloring using anti-rank and maximum-degree parameters and relate it to dual cover decomposition \cite{li2018polychromatic}. The invariant, fiber formulation, hardness source, and exponent are established combinatorial results. The semantic result here is the explicit reduction with its preservation, attack-closure, and source-access obligations, including the directed form and the finite-edge boundary. The tagged realization establishes expressiveness rather than naturalness. The arithmetic fragment adds a structured application with actual local rewrites and reachable representatives; its cube capacity and syndrome construction likewise use known combinatorics. This distinction limits the language claim to the interfaces and mechanisms actually derived here.

The coloring in Equation~\eqref{eq:polychromatic} is a standard
\emph{polychromatic coloring}: every hyperedge must contain every color.  Its
maximum possible number of colors is the \emph{polychromatic number} of the
hypergraph \cite{bollobas2013}.  This established invariant gives the semantic
contribution its target: the exact identification of robust
watermark capacity with that invariant for the incidence structure generated

citation_positions.paragraph:
The newest public mechanisms illustrate why those contracts should remain
separate. SWaRL jointly trains a generator and confidential verifier with
compiler feedback, so its evidence concerns learned generation-time fidelity
and detection \cite{swarl2026}. DuCodeMark protects code datasets with
style-aware trigger--target pairs and repressible poisoning across source and
decompilation tasks \cite{ducodemark2026}. Multi-channel spread-spectrum
watermarking combines naming and syntactic carriers with error correction
\cite{choi2026spread}. Disappearing Ink gives an obfuscation attack on n-gram
detectors under a distribution-consistency assumption \cite{zhang2025disappearing}.
These results address concrete mechanisms or attacks; our question is whether a
fixed behavioral, observational, attack, and access contract admits an exact
source-wise channel at all.

Work on fully abstract compilation includes JavaScript \cite{fournet2013}.
Related approaches use universal embedding \cite{new2016}. A separate line
of work develops modular approximate back-translation \cite{devriese2017}. Robust property preservation classifies guarantees surviving
target contexts \cite{abate2019}. Secure-compilation criteria also address
safety hyperproperties \cite{patrignani2017hyper}. Robust safety is another
such criterion \cite{patrignani2021}. Trace-relating correctness permits different source and
target observation alphabets \cite{abate2021}. Constant-resource compilation
preserves a resource-sensitive relation \cite{barthe2021}. Universal
composability has been characterized through robust compilation in a
cryptographic setting \cite{patrignani2024uc}. Lanckriet et al.\ relate robust
properties, abstraction maps and back-translations across these criteria
\cite{lanckriet2026}. Hyperproperties concern guarantees over sets of traces
rather than ordinary trace properties \cite{clarkson2010}.

citation_positions.paragraph: Cryptographic watermarking demonstrates why approximate and computational contracts require separate analysis. Cohen et al.\ obtain watermarking for cryptographic capabilities under assumptions and relaxed correctness, while also extending impossibility results \cite{cohen2018}. The virtual-black-box obfuscation impossibility literature likewise distinguishes what is observable from code and from black-box access \cite{barak2012}. Our theorems do not imply those computational results. They locate a simpler exact semantic bottleneck that applies before computational hardness is considered.

Cryptographic watermarking formalizes correctness and unremovability against
computationally bounded keyed adversaries \cite{cohen2018}. General
obfuscation impossibility results use computational definitions and specially
constructed program families \cite{barak2012}. Our classifications are
extensional preconditions: an uncolorable fixed-key quotient or access
hypergraph rules out the exact channel before efficiency or cryptographic
hardness is considered.

title: Dynamic Path-Based Software Watermarking
venue: Proceedings of the ACM SIGPLAN 2004 Conference on Programming Language Design and Implementation

carriers, with error correction in Java bytecode and tamper resistance in native code
\cite{collberg2004}.

citation_positions.paragraph: A watermark may preserve ``functionality'' while modifying timing, exception behavior, memory use, traces, or behavior on a rare trigger. Such a claim can be coherent, but only after functionality is defined. Dynamic path-based watermarking uses branching behavior as a carrier and evaluates resilience against concrete transformations \cite{collberg2004}. Semantics-based watermarking makes the chosen abstraction explicit and treats attacks as semantic transformers \cite{dallapreda2019}. The calculus here is complementary: it asks whether the abstraction and attack closure retain enough cells for the desired message alphabet.

Static carriers encode information in source or executable structure. A
Java-class-file construction with source-injected dummy methods demonstrated embedding and extraction under ordinary
program manipulation \cite{monden2000}. Control-flow watermarking made graph
recovery part of detection \cite{venkatesan2001}. Dynamic carriers instead use
execution paths or runtime state. Threaded watermarking encodes and recognizes a
bit string through thread contention \cite{nagra2004}. Opaque-predicate
watermarking exposed the gap between an available carrier and a label that
survives transformation \cite{myles2006}. Path-based watermarking uses runtime branch
carriers, with error correction in Java bytecode and tamper resistance in native code
\cite{collberg2004}. Dynamic graph fingerprinting based resilience on the
difficulty of reconstructing an execution-time alias structure
\cite{collberg2007fingerprinting}. These mechanisms supply candidate outputs,
but they do not by themselves prove that every source reaches every decoder
label required by a universal message alphabet.

current_attributed_claims: Dynamic path-based watermarking uses branching behavior as a carrier and evaluates resilience against concrete transformations \cite{collberg2004}.

Path-based watermarking uses runtime branch
carriers, with error correction in Java bytecode and tamper resistance in native code
\cite{collberg2004}.

current_source_support.version: Final TOPLAS29(6)Article35,67PDFpages,DOI10.1145/1286821.1286826; author-hosted finalPDF in boundpeerretrieval
current_source_support.actual_inspected_section_page: PDF2-4 printed35:2-4 Sections1.1-1.3; PDF17 printed35:17 graph construction/extraction andpointer-alias-analysis motivation; PDF40 printed35:40 Section4.4 limitations/futurework

citation_positions.paragraph:
Static carriers encode information in source or executable structure. A
Java-class-file construction with source-injected dummy methods demonstrated embedding and extraction under ordinary
program manipulation \cite{monden2000}. Control-flow watermarking made graph
recovery part of detection \cite{venkatesan2001}. Dynamic carriers instead use
execution paths or runtime state. Threaded watermarking encodes and recognizes a
bit string through thread contention \cite{nagra2004}. Opaque-predicate
watermarking exposed the gap between an available carrier and a label that
survives transformation \cite{myles2006}. Path-based watermarking uses runtime branch
carriers, with error correction in Java bytecode and tamper resistance in native code
\cite{collberg2004}. Dynamic graph fingerprinting based resilience on the
difficulty of reconstructing an execution-time alias structure
\cite{collberg2007fingerprinting}. These mechanisms supply candidate outputs,
but they do not by themselves prove that every source reaches every decoder
label required by a universal message alphabet.

Dynamic graph fingerprinting based resilience on the
difficulty of reconstructing an execution-time alias structure
\cite{collberg2007fingerprinting}.

citation_positions.paragraph: Program transformations are commonly justified by relational correctness arguments. Abstract interpretation provides a systematic language for sound approximations and transformations \cite{cousot1977}. Relational program logics can prove that transformations preserve specified observations \cite{benton2004}. Secure-compilation criteria strengthen correctness by requiring target contexts not to introduce source-impossible behaviors; trace-relating formulations make the source-target observation relation explicit \cite{abate2021}. Robustly safe compilation focuses on preserving safety properties against adversarial contexts \cite{patrignani2021}.

Abstract interpretation gives a lattice-theoretic account of sound
approximation \cite{cousot1977}. Systematic analysis separates a concrete
semantics, an abstraction, and justified transfer functions \cite{cousot1979}.
The same methodology organizes semantics-preserving transformations
\cite{cousot2002}. Relational proofs can establish that a transformation
preserves the client-selected semantics \cite{benton2004}. Such a proof
discharges $B$ or $\Beh$; it does not determine the implementation image $R$.

current_attributed_claims: Abstract interpretation provides a systematic language for sound approximations and transformations \cite{cousot1977}.

Abstract interpretation gives a lattice-theoretic account of sound
approximation \cite{cousot1977}.

citation_positions.paragraph: A watermark may preserve ``functionality'' while modifying timing, exception behavior, memory use, traces, or behavior on a rare trigger. Such a claim can be coherent, but only after functionality is defined. Dynamic path-based watermarking uses branching behavior as a carrier and evaluates resilience against concrete transformations \cite{collberg2004}. Semantics-based watermarking makes the chosen abstraction explicit and treats attacks as semantic transformers \cite{dallapreda2019}. The calculus here is complementary: it asks whether the abstraction and attack closure retain enough cells for the desired message alphabet.

The closest semantic work makes the abstraction preserved by a watermark part
of its specification. Abstract-interpretation-based watermarking exposes both
the semantic abstraction and the effect of attacks \cite{cousot2004watermark}.
Later formulations relate watermark correctness to selected program
abstractions \cite{dallapreda2017}. An extended account formalizes secrecy,
resilience, transparency, and accuracy through abstraction and completeness
conditions \cite{dallapreda2019}. Loop-structure watermarking gives a concrete
case in which a structural abstraction changes while a chosen semantic
abstraction is preserved \cite{dallapreda2008}. We begin once such a
preservation relation has been justified: detector and attack equalities are
closed into one operational quotient, access is indexed by source, and capacity
is the largest alphabet simultaneously available from every source.

Universal source--signature quantification is not new here: Dalla Preda and
Pasqua already require it in their watermark-system definition and separately
define accuracy through observational equivalence \cite{dallapreda2019}.
Their Section~3.2 leaves data rate dependent on the implementation of the
stegomarker. Our incidence classification instead takes the complete admissible
source image as a parameter and maximizes the common exact alphabet over its
operational cells. It does not replace their secrecy, transparency or
attacker-completeness guarantees, and it does not show that those frameworks
could not express the same finite constraints.

citation_positions.paragraph: A watermark may preserve ``functionality'' while modifying timing, exception behavior, memory use, traces, or behavior on a rare trigger. Such a claim can be coherent, but only after functionality is defined. Dynamic path-based watermarking uses branching behavior as a carrier and evaluates resilience against concrete transformations \cite{collberg2004}. Semantics-based watermarking makes the chosen abstraction explicit and treats attacks as semantic transformers \cite{dallapreda2019}. The calculus here is complementary: it asks whether the abstraction and attack closure retain enough cells for the desired message alphabet.

The closest semantic work makes the abstraction preserved by a watermark part
of its specification. Abstract-interpretation-based watermarking exposes both
the semantic abstraction and the effect of attacks \cite{cousot2004watermark}.
Later formulations relate watermark correctness to selected program
abstractions \cite{dallapreda2017}. An extended account formalizes secrecy,
resilience, transparency, and accuracy through abstraction and completeness
conditions \cite{dallapreda2019}. Loop-structure watermarking gives a concrete
case in which a structural abstraction changes while a chosen semantic
abstraction is preserved \cite{dallapreda2008}. We begin once such a
preservation relation has been justified: detector and attack equalities are
closed into one operational quotient, access is indexed by source, and capacity
is the largest alphabet simultaneously available from every source.

Universal source--signature quantification is not new here: Dalla Preda and
Pasqua already require it in their watermark-system definition and separately
define accuracy through observational equivalence \cite{dallapreda2019}.
Their Section~3.2 leaves data rate dependent on the implementation of the
stegomarker. Our incidence classification instead takes the complete admissible
source image as a parameter and maximizes the common exact alphabet over its
operational cells. It does not replace their secrecy, transparency or
attacker-completeness guarantees, and it does not show that those frameworks
could not express the same finite constraints.

citation_positions.paragraph:
For hardness, reduce from monotone not-all-equal 3-SAT with exactly three
distinct variables per clause, which is NP-complete even under stronger
bounded-occurrence and linearity restrictions \cite{darmann2020}. Given its
variables $V$ and clauses $e\subseteq V$, apply the incidence construction of
Proposition~\ref{prop:incidence-realization}. Labeling an operational class
zero or one is exactly assigning the corresponding variable false or true. A
behavior hyperedge contains both labels exactly when its clause is not all
equal. Hence the formula is satisfiable if and only if the constructed
watermark instance admits an exact bit. Each behavior class intersects the
three operational classes named by its clause. The reduction creates
$\sum_e|e|$ programs and linearly many block-list entries; encodings that list
all equivalent pairs may be quadratic but remain polynomial.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}
Membership in NP is witnessed by a binary label for every $J$-class; each
program's access edge can be checked in polynomial time. For hardness, use the
same monotone distinct-variable not-all-equal 3-SAT source
\cite{darmann2020}. Apply the incidence construction of
Proposition~\ref{prop:access-realization} to its clauses. A color on a
$J$-class is a truth value for the corresponding variable, and every incidence
of a clause has access to exactly that clause's three variable classes. The
access edge contains both colors exactly when the clause is not all equal. The
construction is linear in incidences under the stated block/adjacency-list
encodings and polynomial under standard explicit relation encodings.
\end{proof}

The crossing and access classifications use polychromatic hypergraph coloring,
which places every color in every edge \cite{bollobas2013}. Positive
not-all-equal satisfiability supplies the standard hardness source
\cite{schaefer1978}. Restricted positive variants retain hardness under simple
clause shapes \cite{darmann2020}. These established results supply the combinatorial tools for the semantic classification.
Decoder fibers as transversal partitions are the dual cover-decomposition formulation, not a separate invariant. The product exponent follows already from the general minimum-degree/maximum-edge-size cover bound and duality \cite{bollobas2013}. Li and Zhang formulate polychromatic coloring using anti-rank and maximum-degree parameters and relate it to dual cover decomposition \cite{li2018polychromatic}. The invariant, fiber formulation, hardness source, and exponent are established combinatorial results. The semantic result here is the explicit reduction with its preservation, attack-closure, and source-access obligations, including the directed form and the finite-edge boundary. The tagged realization establishes expressiveness rather than naturalness. The arithmetic fragment adds a structured application with actual local rewrites and reachable representatives; its cube capacity and syndrome construction likewise use known combinatorics. This distinction limits the language claim to the interfaces and mechanisms actually derived here.

For hardness, reduce from monotone not-all-equal 3-SAT with exactly three
distinct variables per clause, which is NP-complete even under stronger
bounded-occurrence and linearity restrictions \cite{darmann2020}. Given its
variables $V$ and clauses $e\subseteq V$, apply the incidence construction of
Proposition~\ref{prop:incidence-realization}. Labeling an operational class
zero or one is exactly assigning the corresponding variable false or true. A
behavior hyperedge contains both labels exactly when its clause is not all
equal. Hence the formula is satisfiable if and only if the constructed
watermark instance admits an exact bit. Each behavior class intersects the
three operational classes named by its clause. The reduction creates
$\sum_e|e|$ programs and linearly many block-list entries; encodings that list
all equivalent pairs may be quadratic but remain polynomial.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}
Membership in NP is witnessed by a binary label for every $J$-class; each
program's access edge can be checked in polynomial time. For hardness, use the
same monotone distinct-variable not-all-equal 3-SAT source
\cite{darmann2020}. Apply the incidence construction of
Proposition~\ref{prop:access-realization} to its clauses. A color on a
$J$-class is a truth value for the corresponding variable, and every incidence
of a clause has access to exactly that clause's three variable classes. The
access edge contains both colors exactly when the clause is not all equal. The
construction is linear in incidences under the stated block/adjacency-list
encodings and polynomial under standard explicit relation encodings.
\end{proof}

The crossing and access classifications use polychromatic hypergraph coloring,
which places every color in every edge \cite{bollobas2013}. Positive
not-all-equal satisfiability supplies the standard hardness source
\cite{schaefer1978}. Restricted positive variants retain hardness under simple
clause shapes \cite{darmann2020}. These established results supply the combinatorial tools for the semantic classification.
Decoder fibers as transversal partitions are the dual cover-decomposition formulation, not a separate invariant. The product exponent follows already from the general minimum-degree/maximum-edge-size cover bound and duality \cite{bollobas2013}. Li and Zhang formulate polychromatic coloring using anti-rank and maximum-degree parameters and relate it to dual cover decomposition \cite{li2018polychromatic}. The invariant, fiber formulation, hardness source, and exponent are established combinatorial results. The semantic result here is the explicit reduction with its preservation, attack-closure, and source-access obligations, including the directed form and the finite-edge boundary. The tagged realization establishes expressiveness rather than naturalness. The arithmetic fragment adds a structured application with actual local rewrites and reachable representatives; its cube capacity and syndrome construction likewise use known combinatorics. This distinction limits the language claim to the interfaces and mechanisms actually derived here.

citation_positions.paragraph: Contextual equivalence has long served as the extensional criterion for program interchangeability. Plotkin's account of LCF connected operational and denotational reasoning about observable behavior \cite{plotkin1977}. Milner characterizes full abstraction by agreement between denotational equality and contextual indistinguishability \cite{milner1977}. For higher-order languages, bisimulation methods provide tractable proof principles for contextual equivalence; Howe's method is a canonical congruence technique \cite{howe1996}. Process-testing equivalences similarly expose how the chosen experiment class determines observational identity \cite{denicola1984}.

Contextual equivalence is the kernel of the observations allowed by a language
contract. Operational accounts of functional languages made contextual
behavior a primary semantic object \cite{plotkin1977}. Full abstraction
requires denotational equality to coincide with contextual equality
\cite{milner1977}. For lazy lambda calculus, convergence-based contextual
equivalence makes the allowed program tests explicit \cite{abramsky1990lazy}. Equivalence
for effectful functional languages shows that the chosen effects materially
change it \cite{mason1991}. Testing equivalence exposes the experiment class
directly for processes \cite{denicola1984}. Algebraic laws for nondeterminism
characterize consequences of those observations compositionally
\cite{hennessy1985}.

citation_positions.paragraph:
Work on fully abstract compilation includes JavaScript \cite{fournet2013}.
Related approaches use universal embedding \cite{new2016}. A separate line
of work develops modular approximate back-translation \cite{devriese2017}. Robust property preservation classifies guarantees surviving
target contexts \cite{abate2019}. Secure-compilation criteria also address
safety hyperproperties \cite{patrignani2017hyper}. Robust safety is another
such criterion \cite{patrignani2021}. Trace-relating correctness permits different source and
target observation alphabets \cite{abate2021}. Constant-resource compilation
preserves a resource-sensitive relation \cite{barthe2021}. Universal
composability has been characterized through robust compilation in a
cryptographic setting \cite{patrignani2024uc}. Lanckriet et al.\ relate robust
properties, abstraction maps and back-translations across these criteria
\cite{lanckriet2026}. Hyperproperties concern guarantees over sets of traces
rather than ordinary trace properties \cite{clarkson2010}.

of work develops modular approximate back-translation \cite{devriese2017}.

citation_positions.paragraph:
Full abstraction has long served as a compiler-security criterion. A compiler
to JavaScript was proved fully abstract by mediating source and target
observations \cite{fournet2013}. Universal embedding gave a reusable
construction principle \cite{new2016}. Approximate back-translation made full
abstraction modular when exact target-to-source simulation was unavailable
\cite{devriese2017}. Robust property preservation broadened the design space by
classifying property classes that survive arbitrary target contexts
\cite{abate2019}. Secure compilation and hyperproperty preservation made the
connection to safety hyperproperties explicit \cite{patrignani2017hyper}.
Robustly safe compilation isolated a criterion focused on robust safety
\cite{patrignani2021}. Trace-relating correctness permits different source and
target observation alphabets \cite{abate2021}. Constant-resource compilation
preserves a resource-sensitive relation rather than only functionality
\cite{barthe2021}. Universal composability has been characterized through
robust compilation in a cryptographic setting \cite{patrignani2024uc}. A
recent synthesis relates robust properties, abstraction maps, and
back-translations across these criteria \cite{lanckriet2026}.

Approximate back-translation made full
abstraction modular when exact target-to-source simulation was unavailable
\cite{devriese2017}.

citation_positions.paragraph:
Full abstraction has long served as a compiler-security criterion. A compiler
to JavaScript was proved fully abstract by mediating source and target
observations \cite{fournet2013}. Universal embedding gave a reusable
construction principle \cite{new2016}. Approximate back-translation made full
abstraction modular when exact target-to-source simulation was unavailable
\cite{devriese2017}. Robust property preservation broadened the design space by
classifying property classes that survive arbitrary target contexts
\cite{abate2019}. Secure compilation and hyperproperty preservation made the
connection to safety hyperproperties explicit \cite{patrignani2017hyper}.
Robustly safe compilation isolated a criterion focused on robust safety
\cite{patrignani2021}. Trace-relating correctness permits different source and
target observation alphabets \cite{abate2021}. Constant-resource compilation
preserves a resource-sensitive relation rather than only functionality
\cite{barthe2021}. Universal composability has been characterized through
robust compilation in a cryptographic setting \cite{patrignani2024uc}. A
recent synthesis relates robust properties, abstraction maps, and
back-translations across these criteria \cite{lanckriet2026}.

observations \cite{fournet2013}.

title: A Proof System for Abstract Non-Interference
venue: Journal of Logic and Computation
hash_basis: exact local BibTeX entry bytes, excluding surrounding blank lines
support_paraphrase:

\cite{giacobazzi2010}.

current_source_support.version: Institutional original author manuscript; final pagination not claimed; selected complete Section5 introductory passage indexed as manuscriptp28
current_source_support.actual_inspected_section_page: Manuscriptp28 Section5 An Application to Language-Based Security: attribute-independent input/output abstractions, narrow versus abstract non-interference, deterministic-program restriction and declassification caveat

citation_positions.paragraph:
Completeness of abstract interpretation characterizes when an abstraction loses
no information relevant to selected operations \cite{giacobazzi2000}. Strong
preservation characterizes abstractions that retain exactly the formulas of an
observation language \cite{ranzato2007}. Abstract non-interference recasts
permitted information release as an abstraction-dependent property
\cite{giacobazzi2010}. Under-approximation results expose structural limits on
nontrivial domains for broad transfer-function families \cite{ascari2024}.
Recent robustness work uses abstraction to weaken classifier observations and
characterize tolerated perturbations \cite{giacobazzi2024}. These lines
motivate stating approximation polarity rather than treating every abstraction
as a neutral implementation detail.

citation_positions.paragraph: Existing mechanisms expose different parts of the model. Transformation-based systems make access a family of source rewrites. CodeMark supplies candidate behavior and attack evidence around adaptive transformations \cite{codemark2023}. DopSteg makes reusable code fragments and constructed branch predicates part of source-dependent access \cite{dopsteg2025}. For generation-time methods, a sampler image can define access only when the embedder may select its outputs. SWEET applies logit bias and detection only at positions above an entropy threshold \cite{sweet2024}. CodeIP adds finite lexical-type guidance \cite{codeip2024}. STONE excludes syntax-critical positions \cite{stone2026}. CLMTracing separates utility-preserving injection from declared removal attacks \cite{clmtracing2025}. Post-hoc CodeGPTSensor supplies a detector relation for origin recognition but, without an owner-controlled transformation, no access relation for exact insertion \cite{codesensor2025}. These evaluations motivate candidate contracts; they do not become exact semantic relations without an explicit proof or interface definition.

Recent systems move the choice into transformation search or constrained
generation. CodeMark selects source-dependent semantics-preserving rewrites and
evaluates harmlessness and robustness \cite{codemark2023}. SWEET conditions
both logit bias and detection on token entropy; it does not remove low-entropy
tokens from generated code \cite{sweet2024}. CodeIP uses grammar-guided
sampling to carry a multibit identifier \cite{codeip2024}. STONE avoids
syntax-critical positions to protect syntactic and functional validity
\cite{stone2026}. CLMTracing separates utility-preserving injection from
removal attacks in a black-box tracing setting \cite{clmtracing2025}. DopSteg
constructs choices from reusable data-oriented fragments and branch predicates
\cite{dopsteg2025}. CodeGPTSensor studies post-hoc origin recognition, which
provides a detector partition but not owner-controlled insertion access
\cite{codesensor2025}.

citation_positions.paragraph: The columns are the standard Hamming parity-check construction: a syndrome difference selects one coordinate \cite{hamming1950}. Here that coordinate is a legal syntax rewrite, not an error to be corrected. For $d=2$ the bound gives $C_2\leq\lfloor4/2\rfloor=2$, attained by the one-column labeling, despite three cells per access edge. For $d=3$ and $d=7$ one commutation selects four and eight messages respectively. On three sites, admitting normalization at one site reduces capacity from four to two; normalizing all three leaves one. With class-complete access the same quotient would instead allow $2^d$ messages. Thus the edit budget and attack closure have distinct, quantitatively visible effects.

citation_positions.paragraph:
Contextual equivalence is the kernel of the observations allowed by a language
contract. Operational accounts of functional languages made contextual
behavior a primary semantic object \cite{plotkin1977}. Full abstraction
requires denotational equality to coincide with contextual equality
\cite{milner1977}. For lazy lambda calculus, convergence-based contextual
equivalence makes the allowed program tests explicit \cite{abramsky1990lazy}. Equivalence
for effectful functional languages shows that the chosen effects materially
change it \cite{mason1991}. Testing equivalence exposes the experiment class
directly for processes \cite{denicola1984}. Algebraic laws for nondeterminism
characterize consequences of those observations compositionally
\cite{hennessy1985}.

contract. Operational accounts of functional languages made contextual
behavior a primary semantic object \cite{plotkin1977}. Full abstraction
requires denotational equality to coincide with contextual equality
\cite{milner1977}. For lazy lambda calculus, convergence-based contextual
equivalence makes the allowed program tests explicit \cite{abramsky1990lazy}. Equivalence
for effectful functional languages shows that the chosen effects materially
change it \cite{mason1991}. Testing equivalence exposes the experiment class
directly for processes \cite{denicola1984}. Algebraic laws for nondeterminism
characterize consequences of those observations compositionally
\cite{hennessy1985}.

citation_positions.paragraph: Contextual equivalence has long served as the extensional criterion for program interchangeability. Plotkin's account of LCF connected operational and denotational reasoning about observable behavior \cite{plotkin1977}. Milner characterizes full abstraction by agreement between denotational equality and contextual indistinguishability \cite{milner1977}. For higher-order languages, bisimulation methods provide tractable proof principles for contextual equivalence; Howe's method is a canonical congruence technique \cite{howe1996}. Process-testing equivalences similarly expose how the chosen experiment class determines observational identity \cite{denicola1984}.

The behavior relation is fixed by a family of contexts and observations. Return values, termination, traces, exceptions, resources, timing classes, and system effects induce different relations and therefore different capacities. A transformation may preserve a partial function while failing a trace-sensitive specification. Positive results need evidence that the selected outputs stay in the declared behavior class; logical relations or bisimulation can certify particular pairs even when contextual equivalence is undecidable in general \cite{howe1996}. Restricting the supported program universe is legitimate, but the restriction must contain every output and attack edge used by the claim.

Howe's method proves congruence for suitable applicative bisimulations
\cite{howe1996}. Sangiorgi isolates their general proof obligations
\cite{sangiorgi1998}. Environmental bisimulation records higher-order observer
knowledge \cite{sangiorgi2007environmental}. The framework also has a
probabilistic extension \cite{sangiorgi2019}. Bisimulations also account for dynamic sealing
\cite{sumii2007dynamic}. They also handle type abstraction with recursion
\cite{sumii2007type}. Step-indexed logical relations support recursive and
quantified types \cite{ahmed2006}. State-dependent representation independence
handles evolving module invariants \cite{ahmed2009}.

title: {SWaRL}: Safeguard Code Watermarking via Reinforcement Learning
venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2601.02602
hash_basis: exact local BibTeX entry bytes, excluding surrounding blank lines
support_paraphrase:
SWaRL jointly trains a generator and confidential verifier with
compiler feedback, so its evidence concerns learned generation-time fidelity
and detection \cite{swarl2026}.

current_source_support.version: arXiv2601.02602v2,7May2026,11PDFpages
current_source_support.actual_inspected_section_page: Title/byline and Introduction PDF1-2; Section3.1 overview and3.2 hybrid reward/GRPO, Figure2 and Eq2, PDF4-5

citation_positions.paragraph:
The newest public mechanisms illustrate why those contracts should remain
separate. SWaRL jointly trains a generator and confidential verifier with
compiler feedback, so its evidence concerns learned generation-time fidelity
and detection \cite{swarl2026}. DuCodeMark protects code datasets with
style-aware trigger--target pairs and repressible poisoning across source and
decompilation tasks \cite{ducodemark2026}. Multi-channel spread-spectrum
watermarking combines naming and syntactic carriers with error correction
\cite{choi2026spread}. Disappearing Ink gives an obfuscation attack on n-gram
detectors under a distribution-consistency assumption \cite{zhang2025disappearing}.
These results address concrete mechanisms or attacks; our question is whether a
fixed behavioral, observational, attack, and access contract admits an exact
source-wise channel at all.

citation_positions.paragraph: Existing mechanisms expose different parts of the model. Transformation-based systems make access a family of source rewrites. CodeMark supplies candidate behavior and attack evidence around adaptive transformations \cite{codemark2023}. DopSteg makes reusable code fragments and constructed branch predicates part of source-dependent access \cite{dopsteg2025}. For generation-time methods, a sampler image can define access only when the embedder may select its outputs. SWEET applies logit bias and detection only at positions above an entropy threshold \cite{sweet2024}. CodeIP adds finite lexical-type guidance \cite{codeip2024}. STONE excludes syntax-critical positions \cite{stone2026}. CLMTracing separates utility-preserving injection from declared removal attacks \cite{clmtracing2025}. Post-hoc CodeGPTSensor supplies a detector relation for origin recognition but, without an owner-controlled transformation, no access relation for exact insertion \cite{codesensor2025}. These evaluations motivate candidate contracts; they do not become exact semantic relations without an explicit proof or interface definition.

Recent systems move the choice into transformation search or constrained
generation. CodeMark selects source-dependent semantics-preserving rewrites and
evaluates harmlessness and robustness \cite{codemark2023}. SWEET conditions
both logit bias and detection on token entropy; it does not remove low-entropy
tokens from generated code \cite{sweet2024}. CodeIP uses grammar-guided
sampling to carry a multibit identifier \cite{codeip2024}. STONE avoids
syntax-critical positions to protect syntactic and functional validity
\cite{stone2026}. CLMTracing separates utility-preserving injection from
removal attacks in a black-box tracing setting \cite{clmtracing2025}. DopSteg
constructs choices from reusable data-oriented fragments and branch predicates
\cite{dopsteg2025}. CodeGPTSensor studies post-hoc origin recognition, which
provides a detector partition but not owner-controlled insertion access
\cite{codesensor2025}.

citation_positions.paragraph:
Observability here is distinct from decidability. Rice's theorem rules out
decision procedures for nontrivial extensional properties of arbitrary
computable functions \cite{rice1953}. Rice--Shapiro results relate positive
semidecision to topological openness in computability settings
\cite{korovina2017}. Our factorization and finite-certificate theorems are
set-theoretic; they do not enumerate contexts or decide contextual equivalence.

The factor need not be effective. Nontrivial extensional properties can be undecidable in Turing-complete languages \cite{rice1953}. Rice--Shapiro-type results connect finite positive information with topology in computable settings \cite{korovina2017}. We now isolate the elementary profile-space boundary used here.

citation_positions.paragraph:
Work on fully abstract compilation includes JavaScript \cite{fournet2013}.
Related approaches use universal embedding \cite{new2016}. A separate line
of work develops modular approximate back-translation \cite{devriese2017}. Robust property preservation classifies guarantees surviving
target contexts \cite{abate2019}. Secure-compilation criteria also address
safety hyperproperties \cite{patrignani2017hyper}. Robust safety is another
such criterion \cite{patrignani2021}. Trace-relating correctness permits different source and
target observation alphabets \cite{abate2021}. Constant-resource compilation
preserves a resource-sensitive relation \cite{barthe2021}. Universal
composability has been characterized through robust compilation in a
cryptographic setting \cite{patrignani2024uc}. Lanckriet et al.\ relate robust
properties, abstraction maps and back-translations across these criteria
\cite{lanckriet2026}. Hyperproperties concern guarantees over sets of traces
rather than ordinary trace properties \cite{clarkson2010}.

properties, abstraction maps and back-translations across these criteria
\cite{lanckriet2026}.

citation_positions.paragraph:
Full abstraction has long served as a compiler-security criterion. A compiler
to JavaScript was proved fully abstract by mediating source and target
observations \cite{fournet2013}. Universal embedding gave a reusable
construction principle \cite{new2016}. Approximate back-translation made full
abstraction modular when exact target-to-source simulation was unavailable
\cite{devriese2017}. Robust property preservation broadened the design space by
classifying property classes that survive arbitrary target contexts
\cite{abate2019}. Secure compilation and hyperproperty preservation made the
connection to safety hyperproperties explicit \cite{patrignani2017hyper}.
Robustly safe compilation isolated a criterion focused on robust safety
\cite{patrignani2021}. Trace-relating correctness permits different source and
target observation alphabets \cite{abate2021}. Constant-resource compilation
preserves a resource-sensitive relation rather than only functionality
\cite{barthe2021}. Universal composability has been characterized through
robust compilation in a cryptographic setting \cite{patrignani2024uc}. A
recent synthesis relates robust properties, abstraction maps, and
back-translations across these criteria \cite{lanckriet2026}.

A

back-translations across these criteria \cite{lanckriet2026}.

citation_positions.paragraph:
Full abstraction has long served as a compiler-security criterion. A compiler
to JavaScript was proved fully abstract by mediating source and target
observations \cite{fournet2013}. Universal embedding gave a reusable
construction principle \cite{new2016}. Approximate back-translation made full
abstraction modular when exact target-to-source simulation was unavailable
\cite{devriese2017}. Robust property preservation broadened the design space by
classifying property classes that survive arbitrary target contexts
\cite{abate2019}. Secure compilation and hyperproperty preservation made the
connection to safety hyperproperties explicit \cite{patrignani2017hyper}.
Robustly safe compilation isolated a criterion focused on robust safety
\cite{patrignani2021}. Trace-relating correctness permits different source and
target observation alphabets \cite{abate2021}. Constant-resource compilation
preserves a resource-sensitive relation rather than only functionality
\cite{barthe2021}. Universal composability has been characterized through
robust compilation in a cryptographic setting \cite{patrignani2024uc}. A
recent synthesis relates robust properties, abstraction maps, and
back-translations across these criteria \cite{lanckriet2026}.

citation_positions.paragraph: Generation-time systems selectively bias sampling probabilities \cite{sweet2024}. Yet these evaluations do not answer the prior question: does every admitted source retain an exact owner-selected channel?

Existing mechanisms expose different parts of the model. Transformation-based systems make access a family of source rewrites. CodeMark supplies candidate behavior and attack evidence around adaptive transformations \cite{codemark2023}. DopSteg makes reusable code fragments and constructed branch predicates part of source-dependent access \cite{dopsteg2025}. For generation-time methods, a sampler image can define access only when the embedder may select its outputs. SWEET applies logit bias and detection only at positions above an entropy threshold \cite{sweet2024}. CodeIP adds finite lexical-type guidance \cite{codeip2024}. STONE excludes syntax-critical positions \cite{stone2026}. CLMTracing separates utility-preserving injection from declared removal attacks \cite{clmtracing2025}. Post-hoc CodeGPTSensor supplies a detector relation for origin recognition but, without an owner-controlled transformation, no access relation for exact insertion \cite{codesensor2025}. These evaluations motivate candidate contracts; they do not become exact semantic relations without an explicit proof or interface definition.

syntax-critical positions to protect syntactic and functional validity
\cite{stone2026}. CLMTracing separates utility-preserving injection from
removal attacks in a black-box tracing setting \cite{clmtracing2025}. DopSteg
constructs choices from reusable data-oriented fragments and branch predicates
\cite{dopsteg2025}. CodeGPTSensor studies post-hoc origin recognition, which
provides a detector partition but not owner-controlled insertion access
\cite{codesensor2025}.

citation_positions.paragraph:
The crossing and access classifications use polychromatic hypergraph coloring,
which places every color in every edge \cite{bollobas2013}. Positive
not-all-equal satisfiability supplies the standard hardness source
\cite{schaefer1978}. Restricted positive variants retain hardness under simple
clause shapes \cite{darmann2020}. These established results supply the combinatorial tools for the semantic classification.
Decoder fibers as transversal partitions are the dual cover-decomposition formulation, not a separate invariant. The product exponent follows already from the general minimum-degree/maximum-edge-size cover bound and duality \cite{bollobas2013}. Li and Zhang formulate polychromatic coloring using anti-rank and maximum-degree parameters and relate it to dual cover decomposition \cite{li2018polychromatic}. The invariant, fiber formulation, hardness source, and exponent are established combinatorial results. The semantic result here is the explicit reduction with its preservation, attack-closure, and source-access obligations, including the directed form and the finite-edge boundary. The tagged realization establishes expressiveness rather than naturalness. The arithmetic fragment adds a structured application with actual local rewrites and reachable representatives; its cube capacity and syndrome construction likewise use known combinatorics. This distinction limits the language claim to the interfaces and mechanisms actually derived here.

citation_positions.paragraph:
The crossing and access classifications use polychromatic hypergraph coloring,
which places every color in every edge \cite{bollobas2013}. Positive
not-all-equal satisfiability supplies the standard hardness source
\cite{schaefer1978}. Restricted positive variants retain hardness under simple
clause shapes \cite{darmann2020}. These established results supply the combinatorial tools for the semantic classification.
Decoder fibers as transversal partitions are the dual cover-decomposition formulation, not a separate invariant. The product exponent follows already from the general minimum-degree/maximum-edge-size cover bound and duality \cite{bollobas2013}. Li and Zhang formulate polychromatic coloring using anti-rank and maximum-degree parameters and relate it to dual cover decomposition \cite{li2018polychromatic}. The invariant, fiber formulation, hardness source, and exponent are established combinatorial results. The semantic result here is the explicit reduction with its preservation, attack-closure, and source-access obligations, including the directed form and the finite-edge boundary. The tagged realization establishes expressiveness rather than naturalness. The arithmetic fragment adds a structured application with actual local rewrites and reachable representatives; its cube capacity and syndrome construction likewise use known combinatorics. This distinction limits the language claim to the interfaces and mechanisms actually derived here.

citation_positions.paragraph: Existing mechanisms expose different parts of the model. Transformation-based systems make access a family of source rewrites. CodeMark supplies candidate behavior and attack evidence around adaptive transformations \cite{codemark2023}. DopSteg makes reusable code fragments and constructed branch predicates part of source-dependent access \cite{dopsteg2025}. For generation-time methods, a sampler image can define access only when the embedder may select its outputs. SWEET applies logit bias and detection only at positions above an entropy threshold \cite{sweet2024}. CodeIP adds finite lexical-type guidance \cite{codeip2024}. STONE excludes syntax-critical positions \cite{stone2026}. CLMTracing separates utility-preserving injection from declared removal attacks \cite{clmtracing2025}. Post-hoc CodeGPTSensor supplies a detector relation for origin recognition but, without an owner-controlled transformation, no access relation for exact insertion \cite{codesensor2025}. These evaluations motivate candidate contracts; they do not become exact semantic relations without an explicit proof or interface definition.

Recent systems move the choice into transformation search or constrained
generation. CodeMark selects source-dependent semantics-preserving rewrites and
evaluates harmlessness and robustness \cite{codemark2023}. SWEET conditions
both logit bias and detection on token entropy; it does not remove low-entropy
tokens from generated code \cite{sweet2024}. CodeIP uses grammar-guided
sampling to carry a multibit identifier \cite{codeip2024}. STONE avoids
syntax-critical positions to protect syntactic and functional validity
\cite{stone2026}. CLMTracing separates utility-preserving injection from
removal attacks in a black-box tracing setting \cite{clmtracing2025}. DopSteg
constructs choices from reusable data-oriented fragments and branch predicates
\cite{dopsteg2025}. CodeGPTSensor studies post-hoc origin recognition, which
provides a detector partition but not owner-controlled insertion access
\cite{codesensor2025}.

citation_positions.paragraph:
Contextual equivalence is the kernel of the observations allowed by a language
contract. Operational accounts of functional languages made contextual
behavior a primary semantic object \cite{plotkin1977}. Full abstraction
requires denotational equality to coincide with contextual equality
\cite{milner1977}. For lazy lambda calculus, convergence-based contextual
equivalence makes the allowed program tests explicit \cite{abramsky1990lazy}. Equivalence
for effectful functional languages shows that the chosen effects materially
change it \cite{mason1991}. Testing equivalence exposes the experiment class
directly for processes \cite{denicola1984}. Algebraic laws for nondeterminism
characterize consequences of those observations compositionally
\cite{hennessy1985}.

citation_positions.paragraph: Contextual equivalence has long served as the extensional criterion for program interchangeability. Plotkin's account of LCF connected operational and denotational reasoning about observable behavior \cite{plotkin1977}. Milner characterizes full abstraction by agreement between denotational equality and contextual indistinguishability \cite{milner1977}. For higher-order languages, bisimulation methods provide tractable proof principles for contextual equivalence; Howe's method is a canonical congruence technique \cite{howe1996}. Process-testing equivalences similarly expose how the chosen experiment class determines observational identity \cite{denicola1984}.

This observation parallels the role of full abstraction in language semantics. Full abstraction aligns semantic equality with contextual indistinguishability \cite{milner1977}. In a watermark contract, that alignment leaves no intra-behavior observational dimension. The conclusion is not that full abstraction is undesirable. It is that arbitrary auxiliary information must live in distinctions intentionally omitted from the preserved-behavior equivalence, intentionally protected from attacks, or both.

citation_positions.paragraph: Contextual equivalence has long served as the extensional criterion for program interchangeability. Plotkin's account of LCF connected operational and denotational reasoning about observable behavior \cite{plotkin1977}. Milner characterizes full abstraction by agreement between denotational equality and contextual indistinguishability \cite{milner1977}. For higher-order languages, bisimulation methods provide tractable proof principles for contextual equivalence; Howe's method is a canonical congruence technique \cite{howe1996}. Process-testing equivalences similarly expose how the chosen experiment class determines observational identity \cite{denicola1984}.

This observation parallels the role of full abstraction in language semantics. Full abstraction aligns semantic equality with contextual indistinguishability \cite{milner1977}. In a watermark contract, that alignment leaves no intra-behavior observational dimension. The conclusion is not that full abstraction is undesirable. It is that arbitrary auxiliary information must live in distinctions intentionally omitted from the preserved-behavior equivalence, intentionally protected from attacks, or both.

Contextual equivalence is the kernel of the observations allowed by a language
contract. Operational accounts of functional languages made contextual
behavior a primary semantic object \cite{plotkin1977}. Full abstraction
requires denotational equality to coincide with contextual equality
\cite{milner1977}. For lazy lambda calculus, convergence-based contextual
equivalence makes the allowed program tests explicit \cite{abramsky1990lazy}. Equivalence
for effectful functional languages shows that the chosen effects materially
change it \cite{mason1991}. Testing equivalence exposes the experiment class
directly for processes \cite{denicola1984}. Algebraic laws for nondeterminism
characterize consequences of those observations compositionally
\cite{hennessy1985}.

Java-class-file construction with source-injected dummy methods demonstrated embedding and extraction under ordinary

current_source_support.version: NAIST deposited author manuscript, not final publisher-byte identity or the separate Japanese journal article
current_source_support.actual_inspected_section_page: Sections 4.1/4.2, encoding/decoding, online original-text lines 95-114/185-211; Sections 5.1/5.2, transformation experiment, online original-text lines 225-253.

citation_positions.paragraph:
Static carriers encode information in source or executable structure. A
Java-class-file construction with source-injected dummy methods demonstrated embedding and extraction under ordinary
program manipulation \cite{monden2000}. Control-flow watermarking made graph
recovery part of detection \cite{venkatesan2001}. Dynamic carriers instead use
execution paths or runtime state. Threaded watermarking encodes and recognizes a
bit string through thread contention \cite{nagra2004}. Opaque-predicate
watermarking exposed the gap between an available carrier and a label that
survives transformation \cite{myles2006}. Path-based watermarking uses runtime branch
carriers, with error correction in Java bytecode and tamper resistance in native code
\cite{collberg2004}. Dynamic graph fingerprinting based resilience on the
difficulty of reconstructing an execution-time alias structure
\cite{collberg2007fingerprinting}. These mechanisms supply candidate outputs,
but they do not by themselves prove that every source reaches every decoder
label required by a universal message alphabet.

Java-class-file construction with source-injected dummy methods demonstrated embedding and extraction under ordinary
program manipulation \cite{monden2000}.

citation_positions.paragraph:
Work on fully abstract compilation includes JavaScript \cite{fournet2013}.
Related approaches use universal embedding \cite{new2016}. A separate line
of work develops modular approximate back-translation \cite{devriese2017}. Robust property preservation classifies guarantees surviving
target contexts \cite{abate2019}. Secure-compilation criteria also address
safety hyperproperties \cite{patrignani2017hyper}. Robust safety is another
such criterion \cite{patrignani2021}. Trace-relating correctness permits different source and
target observation alphabets \cite{abate2021}. Constant-resource compilation
preserves a resource-sensitive relation \cite{barthe2021}. Universal
composability has been characterized through robust compilation in a
cryptographic setting \cite{patrignani2024uc}. Lanckriet et al.\ relate robust
properties, abstraction maps and back-translations across these criteria
\cite{lanckriet2026}. Hyperproperties concern guarantees over sets of traces
rather than ordinary trace properties \cite{clarkson2010}.

citation_positions.paragraph:
Full abstraction has long served as a compiler-security criterion. A compiler
to JavaScript was proved fully abstract by mediating source and target
observations \cite{fournet2013}. Universal embedding gave a reusable
construction principle \cite{new2016}. Approximate back-translation made full
abstraction modular when exact target-to-source simulation was unavailable
\cite{devriese2017}. Robust property preservation broadened the design space by
classifying property classes that survive arbitrary target contexts
\cite{abate2019}. Secure compilation and hyperproperty preservation made the
connection to safety hyperproperties explicit \cite{patrignani2017hyper}.
Robustly safe compilation isolated a criterion focused on robust safety
\cite{patrignani2021}. Trace-relating correctness permits different source and
target observation alphabets \cite{abate2021}. Constant-resource compilation
preserves a resource-sensitive relation rather than only functionality
\cite{barthe2021}. Universal composability has been characterized through
robust compilation in a cryptographic setting \cite{patrignani2024uc}. A
recent synthesis relates robust properties, abstraction maps, and
back-translations across these criteria \cite{lanckriet2026}.

current_attributed_claims:
Universal embedding gave a reusable
construction principle \cite{new2016}.

citation_positions.paragraph: Contextual equivalence has long served as the extensional criterion for program interchangeability. Plotkin's account of LCF connected operational and denotational reasoning about observable behavior \cite{plotkin1977}. Milner characterizes full abstraction by agreement between denotational equality and contextual indistinguishability \cite{milner1977}. For higher-order languages, bisimulation methods provide tractable proof principles for contextual equivalence; Howe's method is a canonical congruence technique \cite{howe1996}. Process-testing equivalences similarly expose how the chosen experiment class determines observational identity \cite{denicola1984}.

Contextual equivalence is the kernel of the observations allowed by a language
contract. Operational accounts of functional languages made contextual
behavior a primary semantic object \cite{plotkin1977}. Full abstraction
requires denotational equality to coincide with contextual equality
\cite{milner1977}. For lazy lambda calculus, convergence-based contextual
equivalence makes the allowed program tests explicit \cite{abramsky1990lazy}. Equivalence
for effectful functional languages shows that the chosen effects materially
change it \cite{mason1991}. Testing equivalence exposes the experiment class
directly for processes \cite{denicola1984}. Algebraic laws for nondeterminism
characterize consequences of those observations compositionally
\cite{hennessy1985}.

Plotkin's account of LCF connected operational and denotational reasoning about observable behavior \cite{plotkin1977}. Milner characterizes full abstraction by agreement between denotational equality and contextual indistinguishability \cite{milner1977}. For higher-order languages, bisimulation methods provide tractable proof principles for contextual equivalence; Howe's method is a canonical congruence technique \cite{howe1996}. Process-testing equivalences similarly expose how the chosen experiment class determines observational identity \cite{denicola1984}.

Contextual equivalence is the kernel of the observations allowed by a language
contract. Operational accounts of functional languages made contextual
behavior a primary semantic object \cite{plotkin1977}. Full abstraction
requires denotational equality to coincide with contextual equality
\cite{milner1977}. For lazy lambda calculus, convergence-based contextual
equivalence makes the allowed program tests explicit \cite{abramsky1990lazy}. Equivalence
for effectful functional languages shows that the chosen effects materially
change it \cite{mason1991}. Testing equivalence exposes the experiment class
directly for processes \cite{denicola1984}. Algebraic laws for nondeterminism
characterize consequences of those observations compositionally
\cite{hennessy1985}.

citation_positions.paragraph:
Completeness of abstract interpretation characterizes when an abstraction loses
no information relevant to selected operations \cite{giacobazzi2000}. Strong
preservation characterizes abstractions that retain exactly the formulas of an
observation language \cite{ranzato2007}. Abstract non-interference recasts
permitted information release as an abstraction-dependent property
\cite{giacobazzi2010}. Under-approximation results expose structural limits on
nontrivial domains for broad transfer-function families \cite{ascari2024}.
Recent robustness work uses abstraction to weaken classifier observations and
characterize tolerated perturbations \cite{giacobazzi2024}. These lines
motivate stating approximation polarity rather than treating every abstraction
as a neutral implementation detail.

citation_positions.paragraph:
Observability here is distinct from decidability. Rice's theorem rules out
decision procedures for nontrivial extensional properties of arbitrary
computable functions \cite{rice1953}. Rice--Shapiro results relate positive
semidecision to topological openness in computability settings
\cite{korovina2017}. Our factorization and finite-certificate theorems are
set-theoretic; they do not enumerate contexts or decide contextual equivalence.

The factor need not be effective. Nontrivial extensional properties can be undecidable in Turing-complete languages \cite{rice1953}. Rice--Shapiro-type results connect finite positive information with topology in computable settings \cite{korovina2017}. We now isolate the elementary profile-space boundary used here.

citation_positions.paragraph:
Howe's method proves congruence for suitable applicative bisimulations
\cite{howe1996}. Sangiorgi isolates their general proof obligations
\cite{sangiorgi1998}. Environmental bisimulation records higher-order observer
knowledge \cite{sangiorgi2007environmental}. The framework also has a
probabilistic extension \cite{sangiorgi2019}. Bisimulations also account for dynamic sealing
\cite{sumii2007dynamic}. They also handle type abstraction with recursion
\cite{sumii2007type}. Step-indexed logical relations support recursive and
quantified types \cite{ahmed2006}. State-dependent representation independence
handles evolving module invariants \cite{ahmed2009}.

current_attributed_claims:
Sangiorgi isolates their general proof obligations
\cite{sangiorgi1998}.

citation_positions.paragraph:
Bisimulation supplies tractable proof principles for contextual claims. Howe's
method proves congruence for suitable applicative bisimulations
\cite{howe1996}. Sangiorgi isolates the general proof obligations behind such
methods \cite{sangiorgi1998}. Environmental bisimulation records an observer's
accumulated knowledge about higher-order values \cite{sangiorgi2007environmental}. Its
probabilistic extension shows why richer observations may require quantitative
relations \cite{sangiorgi2019}. Dynamic sealing has a bisimulation that
accounts for generative protection boundaries \cite{sumii2007dynamic}. Type
abstraction and recursion admit a related proof technique for representation
hiding \cite{sumii2007type}.

current_attributed_claims:
Sangiorgi isolates the general proof obligations behind such
methods \cite{sangiorgi1998}.

citation_positions.paragraph:
The crossing and access classifications use polychromatic hypergraph coloring,
which places every color in every edge \cite{bollobas2013}. Positive
not-all-equal satisfiability supplies the standard hardness source
\cite{schaefer1978}. Restricted positive variants retain hardness under simple
clause shapes \cite{darmann2020}. These established results supply the combinatorial tools for the semantic classification.
Decoder fibers as transversal partitions are the dual cover-decomposition formulation, not a separate invariant. The product exponent follows already from the general minimum-degree/maximum-edge-size cover bound and duality \cite{bollobas2013}. Li and Zhang formulate polychromatic coloring using anti-rank and maximum-degree parameters and relate it to dual cover decomposition \cite{li2018polychromatic}. The invariant, fiber formulation, hardness source, and exponent are established combinatorial results. The semantic result here is the explicit reduction with its preservation, attack-closure, and source-access obligations, including the directed form and the finite-edge boundary. The tagged realization establishes expressiveness rather than naturalness. The arithmetic fragment adds a structured application with actual local rewrites and reachable representatives; its cube capacity and syndrome construction likewise use known combinatorics. This distinction limits the language claim to the interfaces and mechanisms actually derived here.

citation_positions.paragraph: Software-watermarking models distinguish payload, recognition, and resilience \cite{collberg1999}. Semantics-based work makes preservation and attack effects explicit through abstract interpretation \cite{cousot2004watermark}. Transformation-based systems search semantics-preserving rewrites \cite{codemark2023}.

Existing mechanisms expose different parts of the model. Transformation-based systems make access a family of source rewrites. CodeMark supplies candidate behavior and attack evidence around adaptive transformations \cite{codemark2023}. DopSteg makes reusable code fragments and constructed branch predicates part of source-dependent access \cite{dopsteg2025}. For generation-time methods, a sampler image can define access only when the embedder may select its outputs. SWEET applies logit bias and detection only at positions above an entropy threshold \cite{sweet2024}. CodeIP adds finite lexical-type guidance \cite{codeip2024}. STONE excludes syntax-critical positions \cite{stone2026}. CLMTracing separates utility-preserving injection from declared removal attacks \cite{clmtracing2025}. Post-hoc CodeGPTSensor supplies a detector relation for origin recognition but, without an owner-controlled transformation, no access relation for exact insertion \cite{codesensor2025}. These evaluations motivate candidate contracts; they do not become exact semantic relations without an explicit proof or interface definition.

Recent systems move the choice into transformation search or constrained
generation. CodeMark selects source-dependent semantics-preserving rewrites and
evaluates harmlessness and robustness \cite{codemark2023}. SWEET conditions
both logit bias and detection on token entropy; it does not remove low-entropy
tokens from generated code \cite{sweet2024}. CodeIP uses grammar-guided
sampling to carry a multibit identifier \cite{codeip2024}. STONE avoids
syntax-critical positions to protect syntactic and functional validity
\cite{stone2026}. CLMTracing separates utility-preserving injection from
removal attacks in a black-box tracing setting \cite{clmtracing2025}. DopSteg
constructs choices from reusable data-oriented fragments and branch predicates
\cite{dopsteg2025}. CodeGPTSensor studies post-hoc origin recognition, which
provides a detector partition but not owner-controlled insertion access
\cite{codesensor2025}.
